verses.text: In the twenty-third year that Joash son of Ahaziah was king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for seventeen years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. He followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin, and he did not turn away from them.
So the LORD was very angry with Israel. For a long time he let Hazael king of Syria and his son Ben-Hadad defeat them.
Then Jehoahaz begged the LORD for help, and the LORD listened to him, because he saw how badly the king of Syria was treating Israel.
The LORD gave Israel someone to rescue them, and they escaped from the power of Syria. Then the Israelites lived safely in their own homes as before.
But they did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam's family, who had made Israel sin. They kept on doing them. The Asherah pole also stayed standing in Samaria.

The army of Jehoahaz had been reduced to only fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers, because the king of Syria had destroyed the rest and trampled them like dust at threshing time.
The rest of what Jehoahaz did, all his deeds and his power, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
Jehoahaz died and was buried in Samaria. His son Jehoash became king after him.
In the thirty-seventh year that Joash was king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for sixteen years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin. He kept on doing them.
The rest of what Jehoash did, all his deeds and the power he showed in his war against Amaziah king of Judah, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
Jehoash died, and Jeroboam took his place on the throne. Jehoash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
Elisha became sick with the illness that would take his life. Jehoash king of Israel went down to see him and cried over him. "My father! My father!" he said. "The chariots and horsemen of Israel!"
Elisha said to him, "Get a bow and some arrows." So the king got a bow and some arrows.
Elisha said to the king of Israel, "Take the bow in your hands." When he did, Elisha put his own hands on the king's hands.

Elisha said, "Open the window that faces east." So he opened it. Elisha said, "Shoot!" and he shot. Elisha said, "That is the LORD's arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Syria! You will completely defeat the Syrians at Aphek."
Then Elisha said, "Pick up the arrows." When the king picked them up, Elisha told him, "Strike the ground with them." He struck the ground three times and stopped.
The man of God was angry with him and said, "You should have struck the ground five or six times. Then you would have defeated Syria completely. But now you will defeat Syria only three times."
Then Elisha died, and they buried him. Bands of Moabite raiders used to come into the land every spring.

Once, while some Israelites were burying a man, they suddenly saw a band of raiders. So they threw the man's body into Elisha's tomb. As soon as the body touched Elisha's bones, the man came back to life and stood up on his feet.
Hazael king of Syria troubled Israel the whole time Jehoahaz was king.

But the LORD was kind to the Israelites and had mercy on them. He cared for them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He did not want to destroy them, and even then he did not send them away from his presence.
Hazael king of Syria died, and his son Ben-Hadad became king after him.

Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz won back from Ben-Hadad son of Hazael the towns that Hazael had taken in war from his father Jehoahaz. Jehoash defeated Ben-Hadad three times and won back the towns of Israel.
